questions.question: Explain how a hydraulic bottle jack raises, holds and lowers a load, naming the parts involved.
questions.expected_answer: The pump plunger, worked by a lever handle, draws oil from the reservoir through an inlet one-way valve on its up-stroke and forces it through an outlet one-way valve into the ram cylinder on its down-stroke, raising the large ram a small distance with a large force by the area ratio of about 50 to 1, multiplied again by the handle's lever ratio. Between strokes the closed valves trap the incompressible oil under the ram so the load is held without effort. To lower, a release valve is opened, letting oil flow from the ram cylinder back to the reservoir so the load sinks at a controlled rate. An overload valve on good jacks bypasses oil if the pressure exceeds the rated load.

questions.question: Evaluate the hydraulic jack for fitness for purpose, cost and safety, giving evidence for each judgement.
questions.expected_answer: Fitness for purpose: it lifts one corner of a car up to its stamped rated load by about 300 millimetres and holds it; evidence is the rating, the measured lift range and a test under a car; weaknesses are a minimum height too great for low cars, a lift too short for high vehicles, and the need for hard level ground. Cost: a few hundred rand, between a scissor jack and a trolley jack, lasting decades with little maintenance, so highly cost-effective for a workshop though more than an occasional user needs. Safety: it holds reliably through closed valves and an overload valve, but its small base and rigid ram mean hazards of tipping, slipping off the jacking point, slow sinking from a leak and the handle springing back; safe use requires an axle stand, chocks, handbrake and level ground, and designs with a wide base, gripping saddle and clear warnings score higher.

questions.question: Evaluate the jack for aesthetics and ergonomics, and describe how a product evaluation should be written up.
questions.expected_answer: Aesthetics for a tool means looking strong and well made: an even painted finish, clearly stamped rating, machined ram and clean casting signal quality inside and influence buyers; rough finish and stickers signal the reverse. Ergonomics: a two-part handle long enough for lever advantage at kneeling height, pumping force under about 100 newtons so most adults can lift a car, a controllable gradual release, a saddle that can be positioned by feel, and a weight of 3 to 4 kilograms that can be lifted from a boot; cheap jacks fail with short handles and sudden releases. The evaluation is a table with a row per criterion giving observation, judgement and evidence, ending with an overall verdict and two suggested improvements such as a wider base and a two-speed release.
